# cent API reference

<!-- Generated by gen/api_docs.py from cent's docstrings: `make docs`. Do not edit. -->

The public API of cent, from its docstrings. The [README](README.md) shows how to use it; the request and result types come from Centrifugo's protos, with their documentation.

## cent

The client, batches, results and helpers.

### `Client`

```python
Client(
    api_endpoint: str | None=None,
    *,
    api_endpoint_func: Callable[[], str] | None=None,
    api_key: str='',
    bearer_token_func: Callable[[], str] | None=None,
    http_client: httpx2.Client | None=None,
    request_timeout: float | None=None,
    headers: Mapping[str, str] | None=None,
    on_request: Callable[[RequestInfo], None] | None=None,
    auto_batch: AutoBatch | None=None,
    batch_context: BatchContext | None=None,
) -> None
```

Calls Centrifugo's HTTP server API. Safe for concurrent use from
threads, and meant to be created once and shared:

```python
client = cent.Client("http://localhost:8000/api", api_key=os.environ["CENTRIFUGO_API_KEY"])
client.publish(cent.PublishRequest(channel="news", data={"text": "hello"}))
```

Every API method takes its request and returns its result, raising unless
Centrifugo did everything asked. Each takes ``timeout``, in seconds; without
one, request_timeout bounds the call.

Options:

- api_endpoint: the base URL of the API, "http://localhost:8000/api". Each
  method is sent to it plus its name, "/publish".
- api_endpoint_func: instead of api_endpoint, a function returning it for
  each request, for addresses discovered rather than fixed.
- api_key: sent as X-API-Key. Leave it and bearer_token_func unset when
  requests are authenticated another way - mutual TLS, a proxy - or not
  at all.
- bearer_token_func: returns the token sent as "Authorization: Bearer"
  with each request, for Centrifugo PRO's JWKS authentication of the API
  - cent.token.APITokens.token, say. Not together with api_key.
- http_client: the httpx2.Client sending requests - httpx2 is the maintained
  fork of httpx, with the same API. It is never changed:
  credentials and headers go on each request. Without one, the client
  keeps up to 256 connections to a host alive, never follows redirects,
  and closes idle connections after 50 seconds.
- request_timeout: seconds bounding a call without a timeout of its own,
  10 by default.
- headers: extra headers for every request, for a proxy in front of
  Centrifugo. Not X-API-Key, Authorization or Content-Type. A User-Agent
  replaces cent's.
- on_request: called after every HTTP request with a RequestInfo, for
  metrics without a dependency of cent's. It runs in the calling thread,
  and the call waits for it.
- auto_batch: sends calls made concurrently in batches - see AutoBatch.
- batch_context: with auto_batch, makes the context of a batch's request
  from its callers' - for a tracing span linking every caller's - see
  BatchContext. Without it, a batch runs in a context of its own, carrying
  no caller's values.

#### `block_user(request: BlockUserRequest, *, timeout: float | None=None) -> BlockUserResult`

Blocks a user: the user is disconnected and can not
connect again until unblocked or the block expires. Centrifugo PRO only.

#### `broadcast(request: BroadcastRequest, *, timeout: float | None=None) -> BroadcastResult`

Publishes the same data into many channels in one request.

Channels succeed or fail on their own. It returns when every channel
got the publication. When Centrifugo carried the broadcast out and one
or more channels failed - up to all of them - it raises
BroadcastFailedChannelsError, whose ``result`` holds every channel's
outcome. Any other error means it failed as a whole: no channel got a
reply. After a timeout or a network error Centrifugo may still have
published it.

To go on despite some failed channels:

```python
try:
    client.broadcast(request)
except cent.BroadcastFailedChannelsError as e:
    log.warning("broadcast failed in %s", e.result.failed())
```

Retry it with broadcast_with_retry, which sends again only the
channels which may still succeed, with one idempotency_key.

#### `broadcast_with_retry(
    request: BroadcastRequest,
    *,
    max_attempts: int=DEFAULT_MAX_ATTEMPTS,
    attempt_timeout: float | None=None,
    on_attempt_error: BroadcastAttemptCallback | None=None,
    timeout: float | None=None,
) -> BroadcastResult`

Broadcasts as broadcast does, and retries the channels which failed for
a temporary reason - see retryable - up to max_attempts (2 by default:
one retry).

- Only the channels which may still succeed are sent again; when only
  channels which failed for good are left, it stops.
- Every attempt carries the same idempotency_key - made for the call
  when the request has none - so that a channel which got the
  publication in an earlier attempt does not get it again. The memory,
  Redis and PostgreSQL brokers keep keys; the NATS broker ignores them,
  and a retry may publish again.
- The result holds every channel's last outcome, and the key: retrying
  later with it publishes only into the channels which did not get it.

timeout, when set, bounds the whole call, waits included;
attempt_timeout - request_timeout by default - bounds each attempt. on_attempt_error decides the wait
between attempts, and may stop them: see BroadcastAttemptCallback. It raises as
broadcast does.

#### `cancel_push(request: CancelPushRequest, *, timeout: float | None=None) -> CancelPushResult`

Cancels a delayed push notification (sent with
send_at). Centrifugo PRO only.

#### `channels(request: ChannelsRequest, *, timeout: float | None=None) -> ChannelsResult`

Returns active channels (with one or more subscribers).
It can be heavy on large deployments: there is no pagination.

#### `close(timeout: float | None=None) -> None`

Stops the client: calls made from now on raise ClosedError, and close
waits for the calls in progress to end. A broadcast being retried stops
at its next attempt. It raises CentTimeoutError when timeout, in
seconds, passes first; the calls left go on then, and close may be
called again. With its default HTTP client it then closes its
connections.

Call it when the application shuts down, so that what was accepted is
sent before the process exits. A Client is also a context manager
closing it.

#### `connections(request: ConnectionsRequest, *, timeout: float | None=None) -> ConnectionsResult`

Returns information about active connections, without
the need to enable presence. At least one of user, expression or
label_filter must be set. Centrifugo PRO only.

#### `new_batch(*, parallel: bool=False) -> Batch`

An empty Batch sent by this client. Without parallel the commands run
one by one, in the order added - but Centrifugo PRO sends a sequential
batch's publications to its broker together: each channel's take
effect in order, publications into different channels may not, unless
the namespace sets publication_grouping_disabled. With parallel,
Centrifugo runs them concurrently, with no order.

#### `presence(request: PresenceRequest, *, timeout: float | None=None) -> PresenceResult`

Returns the online presence of a channel: all clients
currently subscribed to it. Presence must be enabled for the channel.

#### `presence_stats(request: PresenceStatsRequest, *, timeout: float | None=None) -> PresenceStatsResult`

Returns short presence information of a channel: the
number of clients and of unique users. Presence must be enabled for the
channel.

#### `publish(request: PublishRequest, *, timeout: float | None=None) -> PublishResult`

Publishes data into a channel.

### `AsyncClient`

```python
AsyncClient(
    api_endpoint: str | None=None,
    *,
    api_endpoint_func: Callable[[], str | Awaitable[str]] | None=None,
    api_key: str='',
    bearer_token_func: Callable[[], str | Awaitable[str]] | None=None,
    http_client: httpx2.AsyncClient | None=None,
    request_timeout: float | None=None,
    headers: Mapping[str, str] | None=None,
    on_request: Callable[[RequestInfo], None] | None=None,
    auto_batch: AutoBatch | None=None,
    batch_context: BatchContext | None=None,
) -> None
```

Calls Centrifugo's HTTP server API from asyncio code, as Client does:
the same methods - awaited - options, errors and behaviour.

```python
async with cent.AsyncClient("http://localhost:8000/api", api_key=key) as client:
    await client.publish(cent.PublishRequest(channel="news", data={"text": "hello"}))
```

api_endpoint_func and bearer_token_func may be coroutine functions.
http_client is an httpx2.AsyncClient. A call's timeout bounds it; an
asyncio.timeout around it, or cancelling its task, ends it sooner.

#### `new_batch(*, parallel: bool=False) -> AsyncBatch`

An empty AsyncBatch sent by this client, as Client.new_batch.

### `AutoBatch`

Lets a client send concurrent calls together, as one batch request, once
enough of them are in flight.

Nothing waits for a batch to fill. While fewer than max_in_flight requests
are in flight, every call is sent at once, alone, exactly as without
AutoBatch. Only a call made when max_in_flight requests are already in
flight waits - for one of them to finish, not for a timer. Then all the
calls waiting at that moment go out together, at most max_batch_size of
them. The busier the client, the larger the batches, and the fewer
requests Centrifugo handles for the same work.

Every call gets its own command's reply. Calls made one after another keep
their order: a call waits for its reply, so the next one joins a later
batch. Calls sharing a batch were made concurrently, with no order between
them, and Centrifugo runs them in parallel.

Calls sharing a batch share its request, though: when it fails as a whole
- the network, the credentials, a body too large for a proxy in front of
Centrifugo (nginx refuses bodies over 1 MB by default) - every call in it
fails with that error. Each call keeps its own timeout: the batch lasts
until the latest of its calls'.

A smaller max_in_flight batches more: a value above the concurrency the
load needs leaves nearly every call sent alone. Something like 8 suits
most applications.

- `max_in_flight: int` - How many requests may be in flight before calls start to wait and be batched.
- `max_batch_size: int = _core.DEFAULT_MAX_BATCH_SIZE` - The most calls one batch carries.

### `Batch`

```python
Batch(client: Client, parallel: bool) -> None
```

Commands sent to Centrifugo in one request. Create one with
Client.new_batch, add commands with its methods - one per API method, each
returning a Pending - then call send:

```python
batch = client.new_batch()
pub = batch.publish(cent.PublishRequest(channel="news", data={"text": "hi"}))
stats = batch.presence_stats(cent.PresenceStatsRequest(channel="news"))
batch.send()  # raises unless every command succeeded
pub.result()
```

A batch is sent once, and is not safe for concurrent use.

#### `send(*, timeout: float | None=None) -> BatchResult`

Sends the batch and waits for Centrifugo's reply to every command.

It returns when every command succeeded. BatchFailedCommandsError means
one or more commands failed, up to all: every command got its own
reply, each Pending holds its outcome. Any other error means the batch
failed as a whole: no command got a reply, and every Pending raises
that error. A command the client can tell is invalid fails the whole
batch before anything is sent. An empty batch sends nothing.

### `Pending`

```python
Pending(batch: _BatchBase, index: int, get: Callable[[dict[str, Any]], _T]) -> None
```

The outcome of one command of a batch, available once the batch is sent.

#### `result() -> _T`

The command's result, or its error raised: an ApiError for this
command, the error which failed the whole batch, or BatchNotSentError.
A broadcast raises BroadcastFailedChannelsError, carrying every
channel's outcome, when any channel failed.

### `BatchResult`

```python
BatchResult(replied: bool, failed: list[FailedCommand]) -> None
```

The outcome of a sent batch as a whole. Each command's own outcome is in
the Pending its method returned.

#### `failed() -> list[FailedCommand]`

The commands which failed, with their errors, in the order they were
added. When the batch failed as a whole, that is every command.

### `BroadcastAttempt`

A failed attempt of broadcast_with_retry, given to its on_attempt_error.

- `attempt: int` - The attempt which failed, from 1.
- `error: Exception` - Its error: BroadcastFailedChannelsError when Centrifugo replied and some channels failed, otherwise the error of the request as a whole.
- `retry: list[ChannelResult]` - The channels the next attempt sends, with the errors this attempt failed them with. A broadcast to many channels which all failed lists every one: log a count or a few.
- `result: BroadcastResult` - Every channel's outcome so far, as the call would return it if it stopped now. It is the call's own, updated by later attempts: copy what you keep.
- `idempotency_key: str` - The key every attempt is sent with.

### `BroadcastResult`

The outcome of a broadcast: one entry per channel, in the order the
request listed them.

- `channels: list[ChannelResult] = []`
- `idempotency_key: str = ''` - The key the broadcast was sent with: the request's, or the one broadcast_with_retry made when the request had none. A later retry with it does not publish again into the channels which got the publication.
- `attempts: int = 0` - How many times the broadcast was tried: 1 from broadcast, up to max_attempts from broadcast_with_retry, 0 when it was refused before sending.
- `replied: bool = False` - True when Centrifugo carried the broadcast out and replied for every channel, the failed ones included; False when it failed as a whole.

#### `failed() -> list[ChannelResult]`

The channels which did not get the publication, with their errors, in
the order of the request.

### `ChannelResult`

The outcome of a broadcast in one channel.

- `channel: str` - The channel, as the request named it.
- `result: PublishResult | None = None` - The publication's position in the channel's history, when it succeeded.
- `error: Exception | None = None` - None when the publication succeeded; the channel's ApiError, or the error of the whole broadcast when it failed as a whole.
- `attempts: int = 0` - How many times the channel was sent: more than 1 when broadcast_with_retry retried it.

### `Command`

An API call left for Centrifugo's async consumers to make: written to a
PostgreSQL outbox table, a Kafka topic, a Redis stream. See
https://centrifugal.dev/docs/server/consumers.

Consumers take it as its method and payload apart - the outbox table's
method and payload columns, a message attribute - or as the JSON message
``{"method": ..., "payload": ...}`` of to_json (Kafka, NATS JetStream).

Within a partition a consumer keeps commands in order: a channel's
commands keep their order only when every writer derives their partition
from the channel the same way - the channel as a Kafka message key, say.

- `method: str` - The API method, such as "publish".
- `payload: str` - The request, as JSON text.

#### `to_json() -> str`

The command as one JSON message: ``{"method": ..., "payload": ...}``.

### `FailedCommand`

```python
FailedCommand(index: int, method: str, error: Exception) -> None
```

The failure of one command of a batch.

### `HTTPRequest`

A request to a handler, as the application's function receives it.

- `method: str` - The HTTP method, upper case.
- `headers: Mapping[str, str]` - The headers, looked up case-insensitively: those Centrifugo passes on from the client's connection to a proxy, the client SDK's to an endpoint.
- `query: Mapping[str, str] = {}` - The query parameters, the first value of each.
- `path: str = ''` - The path, as the server saw it.
- `raw: Any = None` - The server's own form of the request: the ASGI scope, the WSGI environ, or what was given to handle - for what the core does not carry, such as the client's address.

### `HTTPResponse`

A handler's answer.

- `status: int`
- `headers: list[tuple[str, str]]`
- `body: bytes`

### `RawJSON`

```python
RawJSON(text: str | bytes) -> None
```

JSON text, sent as it is: a payload already encoded - from a database,
a queue, a cache - or encoded with rules of your own (a faster encoder,
dates, decimals). It is checked to be valid JSON when created, and sent
unchanged, number text kept.

```python
cent.PublishRequest(channel="news", data=cent.RawJSON('{"text":"hi"}'))
```

#### `text  (property)`

The JSON text.

### `RequestInfo`

One HTTP request to Centrifugo's API, for on_request.

- `method: str` - The API method: "publish", say, or "batch" for a batch.
- `commands: int` - How many commands the request carried: 1, or a batch's size.
- `failed: int = 0` - How many of them Centrifugo answered with an error. A broadcast which failed in some channels is not counted: its command was answered.
- `auto_batch: bool = False` - True for a batch made of concurrent calls by automatic batching.
- `duration: float = 0.0` - Seconds from before getting the endpoint and credentials to the reply read.
- `status_code: int = 0` - The HTTP status of the reply, 0 without one.
- `error: Exception | None = None` - The request's own error: the network, a timeout, an HTTP status, a reply which is not Centrifugo's, a request refused before sending - or, in the transport error mode, the error of its one command. None when Centrifugo's reply was read.

## cent: functions

### `exponential_backoff(base: float, limit: float) -> Callable[[int], float]`

The wait, in seconds, before retrying after a failed attempt, attempt 1
being the first failure: base after it, twice as long after each next one,
up to limit. Each wait is a random time between half of it and all of it,
so that clients which failed together do not all retry at the same moment.
A negative base counts as zero, a limit below base as base, and an attempt
below 1 as 1.

In a retry loop of your own - a publication retried with the same
idempotency_key:

```python
backoff = cent.exponential_backoff(0.1, 2.0)
for attempt in itertools.count(1):
    try:
        return client.publish(request)
    except cent.CentError as e:
        if not cent.retryable(e) or attempt == 3:
            raise
    time.sleep(backoff(attempt))   # await asyncio.sleep(...) in async code
```

Retry a broadcast with broadcast_with_retry instead: repeating it resends
to the channels which already got it.

### `new_command(request: Request) -> Command`

The command making the API call request. The request is checked as a
Client checks it before sending - an invalid one raises
InvalidRequestError here, rather than in Centrifugo, whose consumers drop
a command they cannot run - and encoded.

```python
cmd = cent.new_command(cent.PublishRequest(channel="news", data={"text": "hi"}))
cur.execute("INSERT INTO centrifugo_outbox (method, payload, partition) VALUES (%s, %s, 0)",
            (cmd.method, cmd.payload))
```

### `retryable(err: BaseException | None) -> bool`

Whether a new attempt, with time left, may succeed after err: the error
came from a temporary condition, not from the request.

Retryable are an ApiError Centrifugo marked temporary, and code 100 from
Centrifugo versions which did not mark errors yet; a network failure; a
timeout, also a caller's own; an HTTPError 429 or 5xx; a broadcast or batch
partial error with at least one retryable part.

Not retryable are the request's own errors - an unknown channel, a bad
request, InvalidRequestError - and InvalidConfigError, ClosedError, a
cancelled call, a DecodeError, rejected credentials and an invalid TLS
certificate.

A retryable error does not mean nothing was done: retry a publication
only with the same idempotency_key. Retry a broadcast with
broadcast_with_retry, or only its retryable_channels(): repeating the call
resends to the channels which already got it.

## cent: types

### `JSON`

```python
JSON = Any
```

A payload: a JSON value given as the Python value it decodes to - a dict,
list, str, int, float, bool or None - or RawJSON. A str is a JSON string,
never raw JSON.

### `BatchContext`

```python
BatchContext = Callable[[list[contextvars.Context]], AbstractContextManager[Any]]
```

Makes the context an automatic batch's request runs in from its callers'
contexts, in the order they queued: a context manager entered around the
request, in a context of the batch's own. For a tracing span linked to each
caller's span, say:

```python
def batch_context(callers):
    links = [trace.Link(c.run(trace.get_current_span).get_span_context()) for c in callers]
    return tracer.start_as_current_span("cent batch", links=links)
```

Use only the callers' values: some callers may be gone.

### `BroadcastAttemptCallback`

```python
BroadcastAttemptCallback = Callable[[BroadcastAttempt], 'float | None']
```

Called by broadcast_with_retry after an attempt which failed in a way a
retry may fix, except the last. It returns the seconds to wait before the next
attempt, or None for the default wait - exponential_backoff(0.1, 5.0) of the
attempt - and may log or count meanwhile. To stop, it raises: its exception
propagates, chained to the broadcast's error (``__cause__``), which carries
the result when Centrifugo replied. The wait never outlasts the call's
timeout.

### `Request`

```python
Request = PublishRequest | BroadcastRequest | SubscribeRequest | UnsubscribeRequest | DisconnectRequest | P...
```

Any request of the server API: what Client methods and new_command take.

## cent: errors

- `CentError`
  - `ApiError`
    - `BadRequestError`
    - `ConflictError`
    - `InternalError`
    - `NotAvailableError`
    - `NotFoundError`
    - `TooManyRequestsError`
    - `UnknownChannelError`
    - `UnrecoverablePositionError`
  - `BatchFailedCommandsError`
  - `BatchNotSentError`
  - `BatchSentError`
  - `BroadcastFailedChannelsError`
  - `CentTimeoutError`
  - `ClosedError`
  - `DecodeError`
  - `HTTPError`
    - `UnauthorizedError`
  - `InvalidConfigError`
  - `InvalidRequestError`
  - `NetworkError`

### `ApiError`

```python
ApiError(code: int, message: str='', temporary: bool=False) -> None
```

An error of Centrifugo itself: it understood the request and refused it,
or failed to carry it out.

Centrifugo identifies an error by its ``code``; ``message`` is for people
and may change. Errors with a known code are raised as the subclass for
it - ``except UnknownChannelError`` - and any other code as ApiError
itself: Centrifugo adds codes from time to time, so match the ones you
handle and treat the rest by their class.

- `code: int`
- `message: str`
- `temporary: bool`

#### `from_wire(code: int, message: str='', temporary: bool=False) -> ApiError`

The error for code: the subclass of a known code, ApiError otherwise.

### `BadRequestError`

Code 107: Centrifugo refused the request as invalid.

#### `from_wire(code: int, message: str='', temporary: bool=False) -> ApiError`

The error for code: the subclass of a known code, ApiError otherwise.

### `BatchFailedCommandsError`

```python
BatchFailedCommandsError(failed: list[FailedCommand], total: int, result: BatchResult) -> None
```

A batch in which one or more commands failed, up to all of them. Every
command got its own reply: each pending holds its outcome. ``result`` is
the batch's.

It is not an ApiError of its parts: look at each command's error in
``failed``, or at its pending.

- `failed: list[FailedCommand]`
- `total: int`
- `result: BatchResult`

### `BatchNotSentError`

A pending command's result read before its batch was sent.

### `BatchSentError`

A batch sent again: a batch is sent once.

### `BroadcastFailedChannelsError`

```python
BroadcastFailedChannelsError(
    failed: list[ChannelResult],
    total: int,
    result: BroadcastResult,
) -> None
```

A broadcast Centrifugo carried out which failed in one or more of its
channels, up to all of them. ``result`` holds every channel's outcome.

It is not an ApiError of its parts: ``except UnknownChannelError`` does
not catch a broadcast in which one channel of many was unknown, nor one
into a single channel - the broadcast as a whole is not unknown. Look at
each channel's error in ``failed``.

- `failed: list[ChannelResult]`
- `total: int`
- `result: BroadcastResult`

#### `retryable_channels() -> list[str]`

The channels whose failure is retryable, in the order of the request:
the channels a retry should go to, with the same idempotency_key.
Channels which failed for good, such as an unknown channel, are left
out.

### `CentError`

The base of every exception cent raises.

### `CentTimeoutError`

The request timed out: its timeout, or request_timeout. Also a builtin
TimeoutError, so ``except TimeoutError`` catches it whichever layer's
clock ran out. A request which timed out may still have been carried out.

### `ClosedError`

A call made after the client was closed.

### `ConflictError`

Code 113: the request conflicts with the current state - a map publish
whose version check failed, say.

#### `from_wire(code: int, message: str='', temporary: bool=False) -> ApiError`

The error for code: the subclass of a known code, ApiError otherwise.

### `DecodeError`

The reply is not a Centrifugo API reply. The usual cause is an
api_endpoint which does not point at Centrifugo's API, so that something
else - a proxy, a web page - answers instead.

### `HTTPError`

```python
HTTPError(status_code: int, body: bytes=b'', headers: Mapping[str, str] | None=None) -> None
```

A reply with an HTTP status other than 200: the request did not reach the
API method. A 401 is an UnauthorizedError.

- `status_code: int`
- `body: bytes`
- `headers: Mapping[str, str]`

### `InternalError`

Code 100: an internal error of Centrifugo, temporary.

#### `from_wire(code: int, message: str='', temporary: bool=False) -> ApiError`

The error for code: the subclass of a known code, ApiError otherwise.

### `InvalidConfigError`

A client configuration with a mistake: the message names the option and
the fix.

### `InvalidRequestError`

A request the client can tell is wrong without sending it: one which
cannot be encoded - a payload which is not JSON, in any request - or a
publication without a channel or data. It is never sent.

Only rules which hold for every Centrifugo are checked; everything else
Centrifugo checks itself, and reports as a BadRequestError.

### `NetworkError`

The request failed on its way: a refused or reset connection, a failed
TLS handshake. The cause is chained.

### `NotAvailableError`

Code 108: the feature is not available - history or presence off in the
channel's namespace, say.

#### `from_wire(code: int, message: str='', temporary: bool=False) -> ApiError`

The error for code: the subclass of a known code, ApiError otherwise.

### `NotFoundError`

Code 104: what the request refers to was not found.

A method only Centrifugo PRO has, sent in a batch to Centrifugo OSS, fails
with it too, instead of the 404 it gets when sent alone.

#### `from_wire(code: int, message: str='', temporary: bool=False) -> ApiError`

The error for code: the subclass of a known code, ApiError otherwise.

### `TooManyRequestsError`

Code 111: a rate limit was reached, temporary.

#### `from_wire(code: int, message: str='', temporary: bool=False) -> ApiError`

The error for code: the subclass of a known code, ApiError otherwise.

### `UnauthorizedError`

A 401: Centrifugo did not accept the credentials - the API key or the
bearer token.

### `UnknownChannelError`

Code 102: the channel is not in a namespace Centrifugo is configured with.

#### `from_wire(code: int, message: str='', temporary: bool=False) -> ApiError`

The error for code: the subclass of a known code, ApiError otherwise.

### `UnrecoverablePositionError`

Code 112: the stream position asked for is not in the history any more.

#### `from_wire(code: int, message: str='', temporary: bool=False) -> ApiError`

The error for code: the subclass of a known code, ApiError otherwise.

## cent.token

Tokens: connection and subscription tokens for client SDKs, the JSON Web Key
Set Centrifugo verifies them with, and Centrifugo PRO's server API tokens.

```python
from cent import token
key = token.Key.hmac(b"secret")       # client.token.hmac_secret_key
token.connection(key, token.ConnectionClaims(
    user="42", expires_at=datetime.now(UTC) + timedelta(minutes=15)))
```

See https://centrifugal.dev/docs/server/authentication. HMAC keys need
nothing but the standard library; RSA, ECDSA and Ed25519 keys need the
cryptography package: ``pip install cent[crypto]``.

### `NEVER`

```python
NEVER = Never()
```

An expiry which never comes: for expires_at, a token accepted forever -
and forever once leaked; for connection_expires_at and
subscription_expires_at, a connection or subscription which never expires.
Always chosen explicitly.

### `APIClaims`

The claims of a token authenticating calls to Centrifugo PRO's server
API, verified with the keys of http_api.jwks.endpoint. See
https://centrifugal.dev/docs/pro/server_api_enhancements.

A token passing Centrifugo PRO's checks can call every API method, and it
checks only what it is configured to: the signature by any key of the
JWKS endpoint, and audience, issuer and scope only when http_api.jwks sets
them. So the token must carry a claim no other token carries - above all
the connection and subscription tokens users hold:

- sign API tokens with keys of their own, published at their own JWKS
  endpoint - never the one of client.token.jwks_public_endpoint;
- set audience, scope or both, to values only API tokens carry, and
  configure http_api.jwks.audience and scope to require them. api refuses
  claims with neither.

- `audience: str = ''` - The "aud" claim: http_api.jwks.audience.
- `scope: list[str] = []` - The "scope" claim, its scopes joined by spaces: http_api.jwks.scope is one of them.
- `issuer: str = ''` - The "iss" claim: http_api.jwks.issuer.
- `subject: str = ''` - The "sub" claim: who calls the API, for the application's own logs.
- `expires_at: datetime | None = None` - When the token expires: required, best minutes ahead. Centrifugo PRO would accept a token without "exp" for as long as its key is published, so api never signs one.
- `issued_at: datetime | None = None` - The "iat" claim; None for now.
- `id: str = ''` - The "jti" claim.

### `APITokens`

```python
APITokens(
    *,
    claims: APIClaims,
    key: Key | None=None,
    current_key: Callable[[], Key] | None=None,
    ttl: float=300.0,
) -> None
```

Issues the tokens a Client sends to Centrifugo PRO: its token method is
the client's bearer_token_func. It signs a token with api and reuses it for
half its lifetime, so a token sent has at least half of it left. Safe for
concurrent use.

```python
tokens = token.APITokens(key=api_key,   # its own key, not the client tokens'
    claims=token.APIClaims(audience="centrifugo-api", scope=["centrifugo:api"]))
client = cent.Client("https://centrifugo.example.com/api", bearer_token_func=tokens.token)
```

current_key, when set, returns the key to sign each new token with instead
of key - the key active now, when keys rotate. A key must be published in
the JWKS before it signs: Centrifugo PRO refuses a token whose key it can't
find. claims must leave expires_at and issued_at unset: the tokens are
issued when needed and expire ttl seconds later (300 by default).

#### `token() -> str`

A token valid for at least half of ttl, signing a new one when the
previous one has less left.

### `ChannelsCapability`

Operations granted in channels: a connection may do an operation in a
channel when any of its capabilities allows the operation and matches the
channel. Centrifugo PRO only.

- `channels: list[str] = []` - The channels, or channel patterns, it applies to.
- `allow: list[str] = []` - The operations: "sub" (subscribe), "pub" (publish), "hst" (history), "prs" (presence).
- `match: str = ''` - How channels are matched: empty for exact names, "wildcard" or "regex".

### `ConnectionClaims`

The claims of a connection token. See
https://centrifugal.dev/docs/server/authentication.

- `user: str = ''` - The ID of the connection's user: the "sub" claim. Empty for an anonymous connection.
- `expires_at: datetime | Never` - Until when the token is accepted: the "exp" claim, an aware datetime, or NEVER for a token accepted forever - and forever once leaked, for a trusted service's own connection, say. Required. The connection expires then too, unless connection_expires_at says otherwise: Centrifugo asks the client for a new token, and closes the connection without one.
- `connection_expires_at: datetime | Never | None = None` - When set, when the connection expires instead of at expires_at: the "expire_at" claim. NEVER makes the connection never expire - Centrifugo never asks for a new token - while expires_at still bounds when the token is accepted, on reconnects too. Most applications leave it unset.
- `issued_at: datetime | None = None` - The "iat" claim; None for now.
- `id: str = ''` - The "jti" claim, for Centrifugo PRO's token revocation.
- `audience: str = ''` - The "aud" claim: client.token.audience.
- `issuer: str = ''` - The "iss" claim: client.token.issuer.
- `info: JSON = None` - Information about the connection: in presence, join and leave events, and the client's publications.
- `b64info: str = ''` - Binary info in base64, instead of info.
- `channels: list[str] = []` - Server-side channels to subscribe the connection to.
- `subs: dict[str, SubscribeOptions] = {}` - Server-side channels to subscribe the connection to, each with its options. Set channels or subs, not both: Centrifugo ignores channels when subs is set.
- `meta: JSON = None` - Custom data attached to the connection. Not visible to other clients - Centrifugo never sends it - but the token carries it, visible to the user owning the token: put nothing in it that user must not see. The connect proxy's meta never reaches the client.
- `caps: list[ChannelsCapability] = []` - Capabilities granting the connection operations in channels. Centrifugo PRO only.
- `labels: dict[str, str] = {}` - The connection's client labels: for metrics, targeted server API calls and CEL expressions. Centrifugo PRO only.

### `Key`

```python
Key(alg: str, sign: Callable[[bytes], bytes], jwk: dict[str, str] | None, kid: str='') -> None
```

A key signing tokens, matching the one Centrifugo verifies with. Make one
with Key.hmac, Key.rsa, Key.ecdsa, Key.ed25519 or Key.from_pem.

#### `alg  (property)`

The JWS algorithm: HS256, RS256, ES256, ES384, ES512 or EdDSA.

#### `ecdsa(private_key: ec.EllipticCurvePrivateKey) -> Key`

A key signing with ES256, ES384 or ES512 - for a P-256, P-384 or P-521
key - whose public key is Centrifugo's client.token.ecdsa_public_key.

#### `ed25519(private_key: ed25519.Ed25519PrivateKey) -> Key`

A key signing with EdDSA, whose public key is Centrifugo's
client.token.ed25519_public_key (Centrifugo v6.10.2+), or is published
in its JWKS with jwks.

#### `from_pem(pem: bytes | str, password: bytes | None=None) -> Key`

The key of a PEM-encoded private key - RSA, ECDSA or Ed25519 - as
Key.rsa, Key.ecdsa or Key.ed25519 make it.

#### `hmac(secret: bytes | str) -> Key`

A key signing with HS256 and secret: Centrifugo's
client.token.hmac_secret_key.

#### `kid  (property)`

The key ID written as the tokens' "kid", if set.

#### `rsa(private_key: rsa.RSAPrivateKey) -> Key`

A key signing with RS256, whose public key is Centrifugo's
client.token.rsa_public_key.

#### `with_key_id(kid: str) -> Key`

The key, with kid as the "kid" of the tokens it signs: the ID of its
public key in the JWKS Centrifugo verifies with. Never give the ID of
a key to another: Centrifugo caches keys by ID, and would refuse the
other key's tokens until its cache expires.

### `Never`

The type of NEVER: an expiry chosen to be never.

### `SubscribeOptions`

The options of a server-side subscription in ConnectionClaims.subs.

- `info: JSON = None` - Channel-specific information about the connection.
- `b64info: str = ''` - Binary info in base64, instead of info.
- `data: JSON = None` - Sent to the client with the subscription.
- `b64data: str = ''` - Binary data in base64, instead of data.
- `override: SubscribeOptionOverride | None = None` - Channel options of the namespace overridden for this subscription.
- `server_tags_filter: FilterNode | None = None` - Only publications whose tags match it are delivered. Centrifugo PRO only, which refuses a malformed filter: the subscription fails.

### `SubscriptionClaims`

The claims of a subscription token. See
https://centrifugal.dev/docs/server/channel_token_auth.

- `user: str = ''` - The ID of the connection's user: the "sub" claim.
- `channel: str` - The channel the token allows to subscribe to. Required.
- `expires_at: datetime | Never` - Until when the token is accepted: the "exp" claim, or NEVER. Required. The subscription expires then too, unless subscription_expires_at says otherwise.
- `subscription_expires_at: datetime | Never | None = None` - When set, when the subscription expires instead of at expires_at: the "expire_at" claim. NEVER makes it never expire, while expires_at still bounds when the token is accepted: with a short expires_at, a token which subscribes once.
- `issued_at: datetime | None = None` - The "iat" claim; None for now.
- `id: str = ''` - The "jti" claim, for Centrifugo PRO's token revocation.
- `audience: str = ''` - The "aud" claim.
- `issuer: str = ''` - The "iss" claim.
- `info: JSON = None` - Channel-specific information about the connection.
- `b64info: str = ''` - Binary info in base64, instead of info.
- `data: JSON = None` - Sent to the client in the subscribe reply.
- `b64data: str = ''` - Binary data in base64, instead of data.
- `override: SubscribeOptionOverride | None = None` - Channel options of the namespace overridden for this subscription.
- `allow: list[str] = []` - Capabilities in the channel besides subscribing: "pub", "hst", "prs". Centrifugo PRO only.
- `server_tags_filter: FilterNode | None = None` - Only publications whose tags match it are delivered. Centrifugo PRO only.

### `api(key: Key, claims: APIClaims) -> str`

A token for Centrifugo PRO's server API with claims, signed with key - an
asymmetric key with an ID, published by jwks: Centrifugo PRO finds it by
the "kid". See APIClaims for keeping it apart from client tokens, and
APITokens for one to send with every call.

### `connection(key: Key, claims: ConnectionClaims) -> str`

A connection token with claims, signed with key.

### `jwks(*keys: Key) -> str`

The public keys of keys as a JSON Web Key Set, for Centrifugo's
client.token.jwks_public_endpoint, which verifies tokens by their "kid".
Each key needs an ID - see Key.with_key_id - unique in the set. HMAC keys
have no public key to publish, and are refused, as is a set without keys.

A set is how keys rotate without restarting Centrifugo: publish the new
key next to the old one; once every instance of the application publishes
it, sign with it - from a time set ahead, say; drop the old key once the
tokens it signed have expired. Never give a key ID to another key:
Centrifugo caches keys by ID.

Publish the keys of client tokens and of Centrifugo PRO's server API
tokens - see api - at separate endpoints: a token signed with any key of a
set passes Centrifugo's signature check.

### `subscription(key: Key, claims: SubscriptionClaims) -> str`

A subscription token with claims, signed with key.

## cent.endpoints

The HTTP endpoints client SDKs call: for connection and subscription tokens
- what their getToken callbacks fetch - and for shared poll signatures, plus
the JSON Web Key Set Centrifugo fetches.

```python
def issue(request: cent.HTTPRequest) -> str:
    user = session_user(request.headers.get("cookie"))
    if user is None:
        raise endpoints.Unauthorized
    return token.connection(key, token.ConnectionClaims(
        user=user, expires_at=datetime.now(UTC) + timedelta(minutes=15)))
conn = endpoints.ConnectionToken(issue)
app.mount("/centrifugo/connection_token", conn.asgi)   # FastAPI, Starlette
```

An endpoint answers a JSON object, never cached; Unauthorized - also as the
cause of another exception - with 403, on which client SDKs stop asking, and
disconnect or unsubscribe; any other exception with 500, which they retry.
A malformed request gets 400, a wrong method 405. on_error, when set, is told
of every 500 and 400, with the exception.

### `JWKS`

```python
JWKS(*keys: token.Key) -> None
```

Serves the JSON Web Key Set of keys - see token.jwks - at the URL
configured as Centrifugo's client.token.jwks_public_endpoint. It answers
GET and HEAD, cacheable for five minutes. A set token.jwks refuses fails
here, when the endpoint is built.

### `SharedPollSignature`

```python
SharedPollSignature(
    sign: Callable[[HTTPRequest, str, list[str]], tuple[Sequence[str], str] | Awaitable[tuple[Sequence[str], str]]],
    *,
    on_error: OnError | None=None,
) -> None
```

The endpoint a shared poll subscription's getSignature callback calls: a
POST of {"channel": ..., "keys": [...]}, answered {"signature": ...,
"keys": [...]}.

sign(request, channel, keys) decides which of keys the user may track in
channel, signs them - with sharedpoll.sign, say - and returns them, in the
order signed, with the signature: ``(allowed, signature)``. The keys it
leaves out are revoked: the client stops tracking them. To end the
subscription instead, it raises Unauthorized. It may return only keys it
was asked for: a signature covering another would be refused, and such a
key fails the request with 500.

### `Unauthorized`

Raised by the function of an endpoint when the user may not have a token
or signature: answered with 403, on which client SDKs stop asking. It is
the endpoints' own, named after client SDKs' UnauthorizedError - not the
API client's cent.UnauthorizedError, which means Centrifugo refused the
SDK's credentials.

## cent.sharedpoll

Signatures for shared poll subscriptions.

See https://centrifugal.dev/docs/server/shared_poll. Shared poll
subscriptions are experimental in Centrifugo, and this module follows their
changes.

### `sign(
    secret: bytes | str,
    *,
    user: str,
    channel: str,
    keys: Sequence[str],
    expires_at: datetime | None=None,
) -> str`

The signature authorizing user to track keys in channel until expires_at,
as Centrifugo verifies it: "iat:exp:hmac", iat now and exp expires_at in
Unix seconds - 0 when expires_at is None, for a signature which does not
expire. secret is Centrifugo's shared_poll.hmac_secret_key; user is the ID
of the connection's user, empty for an anonymous one.

The signature covers exactly keys, in their order: a client tracking other
keys, or the same in another order, is refused. The arguments but secret
are keyword-only, so that a user and a channel cannot be swapped:

```python
sharedpoll.sign(secret, user="42", channel="poll:prices", keys=["AAPL"], expires_at=exp)
```

## cent.proxy

The application side of Centrifugo's HTTP proxy: the requests Centrifugo
sends to the backend when a client connects, subscribes, publishes or calls an
RPC, the results the backend answers with, and a handler for each proxy type
which decodes the request, calls a function and encodes its answer.

```python
def connect(request: cent.HTTPRequest, req: proxy.ConnectRequest) -> proxy.ConnectResult:
    user = session_user(request.headers.get("cookie"))  # passed on with http_headers
    if user is None:
        raise proxy.Disconnect(4501, "unauthorized")
    return proxy.ConnectResult(user=user)
app.mount("/centrifugo/connect", proxy.ConnectHandler(connect).asgi)
```

and in Centrifugo's configuration:

    "client": {"proxy": {"connect": {"enabled": true,
        "endpoint": "http://backend:3000/centrifugo/connect", "http_headers": ["Cookie"]}}}

See https://centrifugal.dev/docs/server/proxy.

Answering: a function returns a result to accept the request, or raises:

- ProxyError rejects the request with that error, which the client receives:
  use codes in [400, 1999]. The connect, subscribe, publish, RPC, map publish
  and map remove proxies pass it to the client; the shared poll refresh and
  channel state proxies take it as a failure.
- Disconnect closes the client's connection with that code: use codes in
  [4000, 4999] - [4500, 4999] to tell the client not to reconnect. Only the
  proxies which pass a ProxyError to the client honour it.
- Any other exception, or one a proxy cannot carry, fails the request with
  HTTP status 500, and is passed to on_error for logging. Centrifugo then
  answers the client with its temporary internal error; for refresh and sub
  refresh it keeps the connection or subscription for another minute and
  asks again.

A ProxyError or Disconnect raised from another exception (``raise ... from``)
counts too. The refresh and sub refresh proxies end a connection or
subscription through their result's expired, not an exception. A handler
answers with exactly one of result, error and disconnect: Centrifugo would take
a response with none as accepting the request as the client sent it.

Payloads - data, info, meta - arrive as the values they decode to, and a
result takes them back as they are, or as cent.RawJSON. A proxy with
binary_encoding enabled sends them base64-encoded in the b64 fields, with
encoding "binary"; a result may answer with either field.

Security: Centrifugo trusts what a proxy endpoint answers, and the endpoint
trusts what Centrifugo sends - a SubscribeRequest's user is the user
Centrifugo authenticated. Anyone else able to reach the endpoint could claim
any user. Keep proxy endpoints reachable by Centrifugo only: on an internal
network, or behind a check of a secret Centrifugo sends as a static header.

Centrifugo's GRPC proxy is not covered: generate GRPC code from proxy.proto
for it.

### `DEFAULT_MAX_BODY`

```python
DEFAULT_MAX_BODY = 16 << 20
```

The default bound of a request's body, 16 MiB: far above what Centrifugo's
own limits on client messages let through, it only stops a request which is
not Centrifugo's from taking the memory it likes.

### `ConnectHandler`

The connect proxy: the function authenticates a connecting client and
returns its user and initial state. ProxyError rejects the connection;
Disconnect closes it with that code.

### `NotifyCacheEmptyHandler`

The cache empty proxy of Centrifugo PRO: the function learns that a client
subscribed to a channel in cache recovery mode with nothing to recover, and
may publish the current state - then it returns a result with populated
set, for Centrifugo to recover once more. Any exception fails the request,
and the client which subscribed is disconnected to reconnect.

### `ProxyError`

```python
ProxyError(code: int, message: str='', temporary: bool=False) -> None
```

Raised by a proxy function to reject the client's request with this error:
code in [400, 1999], which Centrifugo leaves to applications. temporary
tells the client that retrying may succeed.

### `PublishHandler`

The publish proxy: the function decides whether a client may publish into
a channel, and may change the publication. ProxyError rejects it;
Disconnect closes the connection.

### `RefreshHandler`

The refresh proxy: the function decides whether a connection about to
expire lives on, and until when. To end it, return a result with expired
set. Any exception fails the request, and Centrifugo keeps the connection
for another minute before asking again.
